faqs.q: How much does a Taiwan Dog cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Taiwan Dog puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Taiwan Dog, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Taiwan Dog cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Taiwan Dog are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Taiwan Dogs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Taiwan Dog need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Taiwan Dog's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Taiwan Dogs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs easy to train?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Taiwan Dogs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Most Taiwan Dogs learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Taiwan Dogs commonly have?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Taiwan Dogs live?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs have an average lifespan of 9–13 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Taiwan Dogs than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Taiwan Dog at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Taiwan Dog puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Taiwan Dog puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Taiwan Dog-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs good with kids?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Taiwan Dogs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Taiwan Dogs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Taiwan Dog need per day?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Taiwan Dogs make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Taiwan Dog doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Taiwan Dogs often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Taiwan Dog be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Taiwan Dog depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: A Taiwan Dog needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Adult Taiwan Dogs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Taiwan Dogs benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Taiwan Dog from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Taiwan Dogs can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Taiwan Dog a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Taiwan Dogs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Taiwan Dogs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Taiwan Dogs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Taiwan Dog?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Taiwan Dog — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
